Miami's cocktail landscape is undergoing a notable transformation, with a new generation of bars moving beyond the rum and agave spirits that have long defined the city's drinking culture. According to Eater Miami, vermouth and sherry-based cocktails, along with classic Spanish preparations, are gaining prominence among bartenders and patrons alike, reflecting both the city's deep Latin American roots and an openness to European influences.

The city's position as a gateway between the U.S., the Caribbean, and Latin America has historically made it a laboratory for blended drinking cultures. For decades, this meant rum-forward cocktails infused with citrus and tropical fruits—spirits and flavors that still anchor Miami's identity. But the new bar openings suggest a broadening palate, one that incorporates vermouth, an Italian aromatized fortified wine that became a modern staple in the mid- to late 18th century in Turin and has since been produced across Italy, France, and Spain.

This shift mirrors broader changes in American cocktail culture, where craft bartenders increasingly draw from classic European traditions. Sherry, too, brings a different profile: a Spanish fortified wine with nuance and depth that moves away from the sweetness and tropical punch that once dominated Miami's bar menus. These spirits pair naturally with the city's existing ingredients—fresh citrus remains essential, and the botanical profiles of vermouth and sherry complement rather than compete with Caribbean and Latin American flavor traditions.

The timing also reflects Miami's maturation as a cosmopolitan drinking destination. The city's metropolitan area, with an estimated 6.39 million residents and the third-largest skyline in the U.S., has attracted hospitality professionals and serious cocktail enthusiasts from across the country. New bars are capitalizing on this sophistication, offering experiences that balance respect for classic cocktail-making with the multicultural identity that makes Miami distinct.

For longtime visitors and residents accustomed to mojitos and daiquiris, the emergence of vermouth-forward bars and Spanish cocktails may signal a new chapter. Yet the best of these new establishments appear to understand that Miami's drinking culture works best when it embraces addition rather than replacement—new spirits and techniques layered atop the city's established strengths in rum and tropical flavors.

title: Miami Spice Back with New Reserve Tier and 300 Restaurants
summary: The 25th edition of Miami Spice Restaurant Months is back from August 1 through September 30, 2026. This year’s program from The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) features three-course prix-fixe menus at a minimum of 30% savings at more than 300 participating…
whatHappening: Miami Spice Restaurant Month returns for its 25th edition, running August 1 through September 30, 2026. The program now features a new reserve tier alongside its traditional prix-fixe offerings, expanding to more than 300 participating restaurants across the greater Miami area.
whoInvolved: The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) organizes and promotes Miami Spice, a signature dining program designed to showcase the region's restaurant scene. The initiative brings together hundreds of independent and chain restaurants offering discounted three-course menus to both locals and visitors.
whyMatters: The expansion to 300+ restaurants and introduction of a reserve tier signals growing momentum for Miami's culinary tourism during the late summer and early fall. For diners, the program delivers at least 30% savings on fine dining, while for restaurants, it drives foot traffic and customer acquisition during a traditionally slower season.
articleBody:
Miami's celebrated restaurant promotion is entering a new chapter as the Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau announces the 25th edition of Miami Spice Restaurant Month. Running from August 1 through September 30, 2026, the program has expanded to feature more than 300 participating establishments and introduces a new reserve tier, marking the most comprehensive year yet for the popular dining initiative.

The core appeal of Miami Spice remains its three-course prix-fixe menus available at a minimum of 30% savings, according to Miami Curated. This pricing structure has historically made upscale and fine dining destinations more accessible to a broader audience, democratizing experiences that might otherwise be cost-prohibitive during peak tourist seasons. The addition of a reserve tier this year suggests a stratification of offerings, likely creating separate pricing tiers for different restaurant categories and price points.

The August-through-September window positions Miami Spice as a counterprogramming initiative to the winter season, when the region typically sees peak visitation. By promoting dining during the warmer months, the GMCVB encourages locals and convention visitors to discover or revisit restaurants during a period that might otherwise see reduced traffic. This timing aligns with industry efforts to smooth out seasonal tourism fluctuations and sustain restaurant employment year-round.

The 25-year history of Miami Spice reflects the evolution of Miami's dining landscape from a destination known primarily for casual beachfront fare to a serious culinary hub with Michelin-recognized establishments and acclaimed chefs. The program's expansion to over 300 restaurants demonstrates both the scale of the current restaurant industry in the greater Miami area and the GMCVB's confidence in the program's continued relevance and draw.

For participating restaurants, Miami Spice serves as a strategic marketing investment that drives volume during a season when the region's heat and humidity can suppress regular customer traffic. For diners, the guaranteed minimum 30% discount creates predictable value, particularly for those seeking to explore higher-end establishments without committing to full-price visits. The new reserve tier introduces an additional layer of sophistication to the program, potentially offering premium experiences at elevated discount levels or exclusive menu options for participants seeking something beyond standard offerings.

articleBody:
Miami Curated reports on five exceptional bars in Miami that embody elegance and refined taste. The guide draws parallels to legendary cocktail establishments found in other major cities, particularly the iconic King Cole Bar at the St. Regis in New York, which has long represented a standard of sophisticated hospitality.

The King Cole Bar, housed within the St. Regis New York at 2 East 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, exemplifies the kind of timeless elegance that inspired this Miami-focused feature. Originally developed by John Jacob Astor IV and completed in 1904 to designs by Trowbridge & Livingston, the St. Regis has maintained its reputation as a five-star luxury destination for over a century. The hotel's enduring appeal lies in its commitment to preserving a sense of refined ambiance—a quality that many travelers and locals increasingly seek out in an era dominated by casual aesthetics.

According to Miami Curated, the selected Miami bars share this commitment to elegance and timeless design. These venues offer patrons an immersive experience that transports them to a bygone era when sophistication and refined manners formed the backbone of upscale hospitality. Even as modern fashion and social norms have shifted decidedly toward the casual, these establishments demonstrate that there remains a substantial market for bars that prioritize atmosphere, craftsmanship, and old-world charm.

The guide reflects a broader recognition that Miami's bar scene extends well beyond casual venues and nightlife destinations. The city's most distinguished establishments cater to guests seeking cocktails crafted with precision, environments designed for conversation and relaxation, and service standards that honor hospitality traditions. These bars serve as gathering places for those who value elegance as a lifestyle choice rather than a fleeting trend.

For travelers and locals alike, such venues offer an alternative to the ubiquitous casual bar culture that dominates many metropolitan areas. By highlighting five exceptional Miami bars, the publication underscores the city's capacity to deliver luxury experiences on par with internationally recognized establishments in New York and other major cities.

articleBody:

The establishment, located in Brickell—Miami's financial district and a key component of Greater Downtown Miami—is leveraging the strengths that built its reputation to compete at a higher tier in the city's sushi restaurant landscape.

title: PASTA: The Model Miami Restaurant

whatHappening: PASTA restaurant in Miami is drawing praise as an exemplary dining establishment, earning recognition for its combination of affordable pricing, high-quality cuisine, and refined atmosphere. The restaurant is being positioned as a model that other Miami establishments should emulate.
whoInvolved: PASTA is a Miami-based restaurant that has garnered attention from food critics and local media. The establishment operates as an independent dining venue in Miami's competitive restaurant scene.
whyMatters: PASTA's success demonstrates that Miami restaurants can deliver exceptional quality without premium pricing or excessive noise levels that typically characterize high-end dining. articleBody:
A Miami restaurant called PASTA is earning recognition as a model establishment that challenges conventional assumptions about the trade-offs required in fine dining. According to Miami Curated, the restaurant delivers on multiple fronts simultaneously: very reasonable prices, excellent food across the board, very good service, and a notably low noise level that allows diners to converse comfortably.

The establishment has attracted particular acclaim for its pasta offerings, with observers claiming it serves the best pasta in Miami. This distinction matters in a city with a diverse and competitive culinary landscape. The restaurant's success suggests that Miami diners are willing to frequent establishments that prioritize quality and accessibility over exclusivity and premium pricing.

What sets PASTA apart from many competitors is its commitment to operational fundamentals. The emphasis on maintaining a quiet atmosphere addresses a common complaint among diners at upscale restaurants, where noise levels often escalate as establishments prioritize capacity and energy over comfort. The balance between affordability and quality execution has proven difficult for many restaurants to achieve, making PASTA's apparent success noteworthy.

The recognition of PASTA as a model institution reflects growing consumer interest in restaurants that deliver tangible value. Rather than relying on prestige pricing or elaborate plating to justify costs, the restaurant appears to compete on the merits of its core offering: food quality, service, and dining environment. This approach may influence how other Miami restaurants reconsider their own operational strategies and pricing models.

The restaurant's emergence as a reference point in Miami's dining conversation underscores the appetite for establishments that perform well across multiple dimensions rather than excelling in a single area while accepting mediocrity elsewhere. As Miami continues to develop its culinary reputation, PASTA demonstrates one viable path forward.
